### **1. Phase 0 and Phase 1 Stabilization Planning**

* **Tool:** Codex, GPT-5, OpenAI coding assistant.
* **Access time:** August 19, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Create a specific plan to solve Phase 0 and Phase 1 of the project-wide
optimization, safety, and simplification plan.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To turn the broad build-baseline and safety findings into a dependency-ordered implementation plan with concrete ownership, parsing, shutdown, reset, profiling, and validation decisions.
* **Content generated by AI:** Produced a staged plan covering real Debug/Release configuration, runtime profiling, transactional content loading, procedural pot and enemy-death fixes, stable object IDs, unique ownership, safe raylib resource teardown, non-cyclic room ownership, complete session reset behavior, hardening guards, focused tests, commit boundaries, and final acceptance criteria.
* **Independent work/validation:** I selected Phase 0 and Phase 1 from the previously reviewed project audit and requested a concrete implementation plan before making code changes.

### **2. Capsule DDA Line-of-Sight Refactor Planning**

* **Tool:** Codex, GPT-5, OpenAI coding assistant.
* **Access time:** August 19, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Create a plan that documents the current LOS implementation and replaces it
with a capsule query using grid DDA, deduplicated radius-neighbor tiles,
candidate blocking colliders, capsule-vs-collider narrow phase, and early
exit. Then apply the completed plan to the project.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To inspect the existing static and procedural collision architecture, produce an implementation-ready DDA/capsule design, and apply it consistently to every LOS caller.
* **Content generated by AI:** Documented and replaced the Bresenham/sampled-probe LOS with provider collider extraction, supercover DDA traversal, candidate deduplication, navigation-revision-backed dynamic blocker indexing, exact capsule-versus-rectangle tests, early exit, and real-query debug visualization for all LOS users.
* **Independent work/validation:** I selected the capsule representation and the required `DDA broad phase -> candidate tiles -> capsule-vs-collider narrow phase -> early exit` structure, including the start position, end position, and bullet radius inputs.

### **3. World Manager Ownership Refactor Planning**

* **Tool:** Codex, GPT-5, OpenAI coding assistant.
* **Access time:** August 19, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Create a refactor plan that separates LevelManager and ObjectManager.
LevelManager should own map topology, walls, static props, and destructible boxes,
while ObjectManager should own enemies, projectiles, pots, orbs, and other
dynamic entities. Use one solid/non-solid status for map objects instead of
separate movement, navigation, LOS, and projectile flags. Put
PathFindingManager directly inside GameManager because it needs information
from both LevelManager and ObjectManager. Add an EffectManager if useful,
move the current GameManager vectors to their correct owners, simplify
redundant manager methods, and recommend a clearer child-manager organization.
Then apply the completed refactor plan to the project.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To inspect the current cross-manager ownership, design the target architecture, and implement the ownership migration without changing enemy balance or UI behavior.
* **Content generated by AI:** Produced and applied a dependency-ordered refactor with non-entity map objects and one solid status, typed ObjectManager ownership, GameManager-owned pathfinding, centralized world effects, split map/dynamic factories, routed level spawn records, consolidated reset/shutdown order, and removed redundant LevelManager/GameManager entity storage. Movement, navigation, LOS, and projectile checks now consume the same LevelManager map-collider source, including the Tall Object.
* **Independent work/validation:** I identified the Tall Object collision-versus-LOS inconsistency, simplified map collision to one solid/non-solid rule, moved PathFindingManager ownership to GameManager, and specified that static props and destructible boxes belong to LevelManager while dynamic objects belong to ObjectManager.

### **6. Demon_THA Enemy Design Planning**

* **Tool:** Codex, GPT-5, OpenAI coding assistant.
* **Access time:** August 20, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Create a plan for a new Demon_THA enemy using the supplied idle, running,
shooting-body, shooting-gun, and idle-gun sprites. Attach and rotate the gun
from its (19,0) root at body pixel (33,28), implement alternating random/LOS
tile wandering, LOS/range and idle-entry Aggro triggers, three timed shooting
and recovery cycles, and add the enemy to the Admin Panel. Then apply the
completed plan to the project.

Refine the implementation so non-Aggro movement uses the running body sheet
but does not draw a separate gun layer, because the normal idle/running body
art already contains the gun. Keep the separate gun only for Aggro and use
barrel pixel (2,10) relative to pivot (19,0). Correct the rotation so the
player center and transformed gun pixels (2,10) and (29,10) are collinear.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To inspect the supplied sprite sheets and current enemy, pathfinding, LOS, layered rendering, factory, asset, and Admin Panel systems, then turn the requested behavior into an implementation-ready design.
* **Content generated by AI:** Produced and applied a plan covering verified sheet dimensions and frame counts, art-derived hitbox and foot alignment, typed wandering/Aggro states, room-bounded explicit-goal A*, random and LOS tile selection, three timed attack cycles, capsule-LOS projectile validation, type/factory/asset registration, and a five-type Admin Panel layout. Corrected wandering to use idle/running body-only rendering, restricted the separate gun to Aggro, and solved the pivot-offset rotation so player center and transformed barrel pixels `(2,10)` and `(29,10)` are collinear while projectiles still originate at `(2,10)`.
* **Independent work/validation:** I supplied the Demon_THA art assets, body and gun root coordinates, wandering and Aggro behavior, timing ranges, transition conditions, three-cycle attack structure, and Admin Panel requirement.

### **7. Codebase Audit for Report Preparation**

* **Tool:** Antigravity (Google Deepmind), Gemini 2.5 Pro.
* **Access time:** August 21, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Perform a complete codebase audit for Voltron: Mission Galra Cypher.
Inspect all .cpp and .h files. Review the application entry point, main game
loop, build configuration, player and character systems, enemy systems and AI,
items, collision detection, input handling, game state management, level loading,
rendering, audio, UI, and save/load functionality. Document the project structure,
core architecture, main class responsibilities, OOP design analysis (encapsulation,
inheritance, runtime polymorphism), and full implementation status for all
gameplay systems.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To produce a complete, evidence-based audit of the existing codebase before writing the final project report. The audit was used to verify what was actually implemented versus what was planned, which design patterns genuinely exist, and what the strongest and weakest parts of the project are.
* **Content generated by AI:** A 762-line audit artifact covering: full project structure and module map, execution flow, architecture diagram, 30+ class responsibility table, 10 inheritance hierarchies, 11 runtime polymorphism dispatch sites, full gameplay systems audit (player, collision, enemies, items, levels, audio, UI), and a 50+ feature implementation status table (Fully Implemented / Partially / Not Implemented / Needs Verification).
* **Independent work/validation:** I reviewed the audit output and verified key findings against my own knowledge of the codebase, particularly the Observer pattern weakness and the absence of save/load persistence.

### **8. Report Blueprint and Grading Gap Analysis**

* **Tool:** Antigravity (Google Deepmind), Gemini 2.5 Pro.
* **Access time:** August 21, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Analyze the Codebase Audit Against the Grading Requirements and Create a Report
Blueprint. Execute Parts A through G:
(A) Design Pattern Audit — evaluate every plausible pattern (State, Strategy,
Observer, Singleton, Factory, Command, Template Method, Object Pool, Facade, etc.)
with Confirmed/Partially/Not Implemented status, formal evidence, and report strength.
(B) Design Pattern Gap Analysis — identify gaps below 5 strong patterns.
(C) Grading Gap Analysis — compare every grading criterion against actual
implementation status.
(D) Evaluate the proposed Table of Contents.
(E) Create the Optimized Report Blueprint with purpose, evidence, grading criteria,
visual plan, and writing priority per section.
(F) Screenshot, Diagram, and Evidence Plan.
(G) Final Improvement Plan with Maximum Grade Strategy.
Critical rule: Do not force the code into a pattern.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To produce a complete blueprint for writing the project report. The analysis was used to determine which design patterns are genuinely defensible, which grading criteria are at risk, what evidence is needed for each section, and what code changes are highest priority before submission.
* **Content generated by AI:** A comprehensive blueprint artifact covering: full 14-pattern audit with formal evaluation; grading gap analysis against the CS202 rubric (65+35+15 = 115 points); optimized 9-section report structure with purpose/evidence/grading criteria/visual plan/priority for each section; 18 screenshot requirements, 13 diagram requirements, 14 code snippet requirements; prioritized 5-step improvement plan with expected grade ranges (95–107/115 with fixes applied).
* **Independent work/validation:** I specified the critical evaluation rule (pattern name does not equal pattern evidence), identified the Observer pattern weakness as the primary risk, and confirmed that the project has exactly 5 defensible patterns without fabrication.

### **9. Complete Project Report Draft**

* **Tool:** Antigravity (Google Deepmind), Gemini 2.5 Pro.
* **Access time:** August 21, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Write the complete first draft of the project report for Voltron: Mission
Galra Cypher. Use the completed Codebase Audit, Design Pattern Audit, Grading
Gap Analysis, and optimized Report Blueprint as sources of truth. The report
must be based strictly on the actual implementation. Do not invent features,
classes, or patterns. Clearly distinguish between Implemented, Partially
Implemented, and Not Implemented. Use the optimized Table of Contents from the
blueprint. Include visual evidence placeholders (screenshots, UML diagrams,
sequence diagrams, state diagrams) and code snippet placeholders for all
verified evidence. Write in a professional software engineering and academic
report style. The report must cover: Introduction, Software Architecture and
OOP Design, Design Pattern Implementation (all 5 verified patterns), Core
Gameplay Systems, Game Progression and Content, Advanced Features, Testing and
Limitations, and Conclusion with a demo video link placeholder.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To produce a complete, editable first draft of the CS202 final project report that can be directly polished into the submission document. The draft was designed to be technically accurate, grading-rubric-optimized, and easy for the instructor to verify.
* **Content generated by AI:** A full report draft (~3,500 words) covering 8 major sections with 35 figure placeholders, 15 code snippet placeholders, and a complete Report Completion Checklist. Key content includes: system architecture diagram description, 10 inheritance hierarchy diagrams, 11 runtime polymorphism dispatch sites table, formal analysis of all 5 patterns (State with 3 machines, Strategy with 4 contexts, Observer with partial-status notation, Singleton with 8 instances, Factory Method), full gameplay system documentation (input/movement/collision/combat/AI/items/levels/audio), honest limitations section (Save/Load = NOT IMPLEMENTED, difficulty scaling = PARTIAL, Observer handler = PARTIAL), and maximum-grade-strategy conclusion.
* **Independent work/validation:** I reviewed the draft for accuracy against my own knowledge of the codebase, confirmed that Save/Load is not described as implemented, confirmed that the Observer pattern partial status is honestly documented, and confirmed that all code snippet references point to verified source files identified in the codebase audit.

### **10. Complete LaTeX Project Report**

* **Tool:** Antigravity (Google Deepmind), Gemini 2.5 Pro.
* **Access time:** August 21, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Rewrite the project report as a complete LaTeX document following a 12-section
academic structure: Cover Page (Group 55, CS202, Class 25A02), Table of
Contents, Abstract, Introduction (Background/Motivation/Objectives), Group
Information, Data Storage, Project Architecture (overall architecture, folder
structure, main data structures), Implementation Details (main classes,
OOP design, all 5 verified design patterns, main system flows), Technical
Problems and Solutions, Features Demonstration with screenshot placeholders,
Conclusion, and References. The document must be compilable LaTeX using
\documentclass[12pt,a4paper]{report}. Use listings for C++ code, booktabs
for tables, hyperref for clickable ToC. All technical claims must come from
the verified codebase audit. Save/Load = NOT IMPLEMENTED. Observer = PARTIAL.
Use placeholders for missing information (student IDs, contribution %, video
link, screenshot files). Do not invent features or code examples.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To produce a complete, submission-ready LaTeX `.tex` file that restructures the verified report draft into the required academic report format for CS202.
* **Content generated by AI:** A full compilable LaTeX document (~700 lines) covering all 12 required sections. Key content includes: professional cover page with group/course/class metadata, auto-generated ToC, abstract summarizing all 5 verified patterns, 3 introduction subsections (background/motivation/objectives), group information table with name placeholders, data storage analysis (CSV tilemap files, in-memory data structures with longtable comparison, session-continue honest description), project architecture section (4-tier system, main loop listing, folder tree, data structure table), implementation details (class responsibility longtable, OOP encapsulation/inheritance/polymorphism with 11-site table, all 5 design patterns with code listings and figure placeholders, 5 system flow descriptions), 7-row technical problems table, features demonstration with figure environments for all major features, conclusion with limitations and future work, and 11 references (raylib, C++ standard, GoF, CMake, Tiled, A* paper, DDA paper).
* **Independent work/validation:** I specified the 12-section structure, the use of Meyers Singleton as the correct pattern name, the requirement to mark Save/Load as not implemented, and the requirement to use commented-out includegraphics placeholders for all screenshot figures. I also confirmed that all code listings in the document reference verified source files from the codebase audit.
